Chapter 6. Zoning Use Regulations

Section 6.01. Zoning Uses
6.01.010. General
      A. Authority
           The provisions of this chapter are adopted pursuant to Texas Local Government Code Chapter 211 and the City
           Charter.
      B.   Purpose
           Section 6.02 is intended to provide a list of uses allowed within each of the City’s Zoning Districts. Approval of a
           use listed in this chapter, and compliance with the applicable use-specific standards for that use, authorize that
           use only.
      C.   Compliance with Code of Ordinances
           Other sections of the City of Georgetown Code of Ordinances, along with other City regulations, may also apply
           to or affect a proposed use in addition to the standards in this Chapter 6.

6.01.020. Zoning Use Classifications
      A. Use Categories
           A primary use is assigned to the Use Category that most closely corresponds to its nature as described in the
           characteristics of each Use Category. Use Categories classify land uses and activities based on similar functional,
           product or physical characteristics. Characteristics include the type and amount of activity, the type of customers
           or residents, how goods or services are sold or delivered, likely impact on surrounding properties, and site
           conditions.
      B.   Use Tables
           The Use Table (Section 6.02 below) depicts the specific zoning uses allowed by Zoning District. The table may be
           further divided by use category, for example "Residential Uses" that contains specific listed uses and their
           corresponding Zoning Districts. All of the uses listed in the Use Tables found in this chapter are defined in Chapter
           18. Definitions . Below is a key to the Use Table indicating how each use is treated by District.
           1.   Uses Permitted by Right
                A "P" indicates that a use is allowed by right. Such uses are subject to all other applicable regulations of this
                UDC and the City Code of Ordinances.
           2.   Uses with Limitations
                An "L" indicates that a use is permitted, provided that it meets additional standards or limitations referenced
                in the far right "Note" column of each Use Table. These standards can be found following each use table.
                Such uses are subject to all other applicable regulations of this UDC and the City Code of Ordinances.
           3.   Uses with Special Use Permit
                An "S" indicates that a use is allowed only if granted a Special Use Permit by the City Council in accordance
                with the procedures in Section 3.10 and the limitations following each use table. Uses that require a Special
                Use Permit are required to meet all other applicable regulations of this UDC and the City Code of Ordinances,
                including the additional standards contained in the limitation section of each use category.
           4.   Uses Not Allowed



132                                                                                     Unified Development Code 2026
City of Georgetown                                                            Chapter 6. Zoning Use Regulations
Unified Development Code                                                               Section 6.01. Zoning Uses

             A cell left blank indicates that a use is not allowed.
   C.   Multiple Primary Uses
        Multiple primary uses on one lot shall be allowed only if each individual use is allowed in the underlying District,
        unless otherwise specified by this UDC or the City Code of Ordinances. Limitations or Special Use Permits
        required of any of the primary uses shall be met or obtained before commencement of any use. In the event of a
        conflict between limitations following each use table, the stricter provision shall apply.
   D. General Construction of the Use Table
        The Use Table organizes uses alphabetically according to one of the following categories:
        1.   Residential Uses
             Encompasses uses intended for residential dwellings and related accessory uses. These uses include single-
             family and multi-family residential structures and accommodate groups of people that may exceed the
             definition of household.
        2.   Civic Uses & Institutional Uses
             Encompasses uses that provide community services to or for the general public. Civic uses are typically found
             in Non-Residential Zoning Districts but may be allowed in Residential Districts, often with limitations or
             Special Use Permits. These uses are generally public or non-profit but also include for-profit entities that
             provide a service to the general public. Civic uses include, but are not limited to, facilities for education,
             daycare, government, social services, institutions, places of worship, and parks and open spaces.
        3.   Commercial Uses
             Encompasses uses that include businesses that facilitate the buying and selling of manufactured goods or
             provide consumer and professional sales and services. These uses may include, but are not limited to,
             overnight accommodations, establishments for food and beverage preparation and consumption,
             entertainment or recreation-oriented activities, out-patient or home-care health and medical services, and
             professional and business offices. A commercial use also encompasses retail sales and service uses for
             personal improvement, self-storage, heavy commercial and wholesale sales and services, and automobile
             sales, repair, and service.
        4.   Transportation & Utility Uses
             Encompasses uses that are intended for public or private utilities and large-scale communication
             transmission facilities. These uses may serve small or large-scale areas with various intensity and nuisance.
             Transportation uses include, but are not limited to, electrical transmission lines, water and sewer
             infrastructure and treatment. Utility uses typically contain light traffic and minimal personnel although some
             larger uses, which serve the general community, may not be compatible in residential areas.
        5.   Industrial Uses
             Encompasses uses that range from light manufacturing and assembly, equipment servicing, storage/freight
             management to waste-related services. Public traffic and on-site sales are very limited. Industrial uses and
             facilities are typically incompatible near residential Districts
        6.   Agricultural Uses
             Encompasses uses that create and preserve areas intended primarily for the raising of animals and crops, and
             the secondary industries associated with agricultural production.
        7.   Accessory Uses
             Encompasses uses that are ancillary or secondary to a primary use established elsewhere by this chapter.




Unified Development Code 2026                                                                                            133
Chapter 6. Zoning Use Regulations                                                                     City of Georgetown
Section 6.01. Zoning Uses                                                                     Unified Development Code

           8.   Temporary Uses
                Encompasses uses with a fixed, usually short-term, period of time with the intent to discontinue the use
                upon the expiration of the time. Temporary uses have characteristics that require certain restrictions in order
                to ensure compatibility with other uses in the Zoning District in which they are proposed.
      E.   Specific Use Terms and Definitions
           1.   The names of the specific uses listed in each Use Table are defined in Chapter 18 of this Code.
           2.   The definition given in the Use Table is intended to provide a general description of the use, in addition to
                any standards or conditions appearing in this UDC that are directly related to the use that the Director may
                rely upon when identifying and defining a use.
           3.   The Use Table and associated definitions are intended to provide a technical reference to each use, and as
                such the terms used take precedence over any non-technical, lay, common, or shorthand usage of particular
                terms, or other housing types not meeting the strict definition of those housing types). The applicant for
                approval of any use is responsible for determining the applicable use and its correct term and definition prior
                to commencing construction or preparation of plans.
      F.   Accessory Uses
           1.   Accessory uses are those activities that are incidental and subordinate to a primary use but customarily
                associated with the particular primary use. The following are two examples of primary uses and some of
                their possible accessory uses:
                a.   A high school may typically include, but may not be limited to, accessory uses such as a cafeteria, library,
                     maintenance facility, meeting rooms, auditorium, laboratories, indoor recreation courts, outdoor
                     recreational fields, and concession stands.
                b.   A hospital may include, but may not be limited to, a cafeteria and a small retail operation.
           2.   An accessory use may be determined to be an allowed accessory use to a primary use if:
                a.   It is listed as an accessory use to the primary use in the definition of such primary use in Chapter 18 of
                     this Code; or
                b.   It is determined to be customarily associated with the primary use. If a proposed Accessory Use is not
                     specifically defined, the Director shall have the authority to determine if an accessory use is customarily
                     associated with a primary use following the criteria in this Subsection 6.01.020.F.
           3.   An allowed accessory use shall be consistent with the following:
                a.   The accessory use shall be subordinate to and dependent upon an authorized primary use;
                b.   The accessory use shall be smaller in floor area than the primary use;
                c.   The accessory use shall be subject to the same regulations as the primary use, unless otherwise
                     specified by this UDC;
                d.   The accessory use must be a permitted use within the same Zoning District as the primary use. In
                     addition, if an accessory use is subject to limitations as a primary use then those same limitations shall
                     apply to the accessory use, unless otherwise specified by this UDC

6.01.030. Determination of Unlisted Uses
      A. Determination by Director
           1.   Determination of the appropriate Zoning District for a use not listed in the Use Table shall be made by the
                Director in accordance with the provisions of Subsection 6.01.030.B below.



134                                                                                     Unified Development Code 2026
City of Georgetown                                                               Chapter 6. Zoning Use Regulations
Unified Development Code                                                                  Section 6.01. Zoning Uses

        2.   When considering appropriate Districts for a use not listed in the Use Table, the District Purpose Statements
             in Chapter 7 and Chapter 8, the descriptive characteristics of each use category, and definitions of similar
             uses shall be considered.
        3.   Upon receiving an application for an unlisted use, the Director may make a determination, based on these
             considerations, that such a use:
             a.   Be allowed by right as an authorized use under one or more listed uses in the current Use Table; or
             b.   Not be allowed under this UDC, therefore requiring approval of a Text Amendment to this UDC prior to
                  receiving approval of the use.
   B.   The following criteria shall be used to determine 1) the appropriate use for an activity not specifically listed in the
        Use Tables, and 2) whether a use is considered primary or accessory.
        1.   The definitions of similar primary uses;
        2.   The descriptions of the use categories that include similar uses;
        3.   The actual or projected characteristics of the activity in relationship to the characteristics proposed by the
             applicant for the use;
        4.   The intensity or relative impact of the use upon the site and surrounding properties;
        5.   The traffic impact generated by the use based on vehicle trips generated and types of vehicles used;
        6.   The relative number of employees for each activity associated with the proposed use;
        7.   Hours of operation of the proposed use;
        8.   Parking requirements for the proposed use. In making a use determination, the Director is authorized to
             apply a required parking ratio that is appropriate to the use, based on the required parking ratio for similar
             uses found in the Use Table;
        9.   Noise levels generated by activities associated with the proposed use;
        10. Lighting required for activities associated with the proposed use; and
        11. Whether the activity is likely to be found independent of the other activities on the site.
   C.   The Director's determination shall be made public on the City's website for 30 days following the decision and
        shall be considered final if no appeal is filed during that time frame.
   D. Appeal of Unlisted Use Determination. The Zoning Board of Adjustment may hear and decide an appeal that
      alleges error in a determination made by the Director in the enforcement of this chapter. In exercising its
      authority under this subsection, the Board may reverse or affirm, in whole or in part, or modify the Director's
      determination and make the correct determination, and for that purpose the Board has the same authority as
      the Director. The appeal process is pursuant to Chapter 3 of this UDC.

   B.   Residential Use Standards
        1.   Single-Family, Attached
             An Attached Single-family dwelling is permitted in accordance with A above, Section 6.02.010.A and subject
             to the following standards and limitations:
             a.   Both dwelling units shall be situated on separate legally platted lots.
             b.   Attached single-family dwellings are not allowed in the Old Town Overlay District (established in Chapter
                  5).
        2.   Multifamily, Detached Dwelling Units
             a.   Detached multifamily dwelling units are permitted in accordance with Section 6.02.
             b.   Detached multifamily dwelling units require a Condominium Plat. No more than one main building is
                  allowed per lot. Each lot must have access to a public street.
             c.   Parking must be located behind a main building and not be visible from the street.
             d.   First floor units must be accessed only by indoor entry within the building.
             e.   A Special Use Permit, pursuant to Section 3.07, is required for detached multifamily dwelling units as
                  designated in the table in Section 6.02.010.A and is subject to the following conditions:
                  (i) The location and context of the detached multifamily development shall be secondary and
                      supportive to established surrounding commercial uses, helping to facilitate an active, pedestrian
                      friendly environment where the mixture of uses enables people to live, work, play, and shop.
                  (ii) Connections within the development must be provided to ensure vehicular and pedestrian
                       connectivity.
                  (iii) Setbacks shall be in conformance with the setbacks of the District in which the detached multifamily
                        development is proposed.
                  (iv) Building height shall be in conformance with the building height of the District in which the
                       detached multifamily development is proposed.
                  (v) Detached multifamily development in all Districts shall also meet the building design standards of
                      Section 8.04, the lighting design standards of Section 8.05, and the non-residential landscape
                      requirements of Section 9.02.
                  (vi) Detached multifamily development in all Districts must also meet the common amenity area
                       requirements of Section 7.05 and the parkland dedication requirements of Section 15.08.
             f.   In addition to the requirements of Section 6.02.010.B.2.e, when reviewing the conceptual site layout
                  required per Section 3.07, the City Council may consider and add conditions, provided the requirements
                  of the Zoning District are not exceeded, to the Special Use Permit including, but not limited to, the
                  following:
                  (i) Location of the development;


Unified Development Code 2026                                                                                              137
Chapter 6. Zoning Use Regulations                                                               City of Georgetown
Section 6.02. Use Tables                                                                Unified Development Code

                (ii) Amount of lot frontage along a commercial corridor;
                (iii) Dwelling units per acre (maximum 24);
                (iv) Maximum building heights;
                (v) Dwelling units per structure;
                (vi) Type and number of amenities;
                (vii) Accessory structures;
                (viii) Ingress and egress locations; and
                (ix) Landscape buffers.
      3.   Multifamily, Attached Dwelling Units
           a.   Attached multifamily dwelling units are permitted in accordance with Section 6.02.
           b.   No more than one main building is allowed per lot. Each lot must have access to a public street.
           c.   Each building must front along a public street or regional trail, except as permitted in Section
                11.03.040.C.
           d.   Parking must be located behind a main building and not be visible from the street.
           e.   First floor units must be accessed only by indoor entry within the building.
           f.   A Special Use Permit, pursuant to Section 3.10, is required for attached multifamily dwelling units as
                designated in 6.02.010 and is subject to the following conditions:
                (i) The location and context of the attached multifamily development shall be secondary and
                    supportive to established surrounding commercial uses, helping to facilitate an active, pedestrian
                    friendly environment where the mixture of uses enables people to live, work, play, and shop.
                (ii) Connections within the development must be provided to ensure vehicular and pedestrian
                     connectivity.
                (iii) Impervious coverage for attached multifamily developments in a C-1, C-2 or I-1 District shall be
                      limited to 50%.
                (iv) Front setbacks shall be in conformance with the front setback of the District in which the attached
                     multifamily development is proposed. Side and rear setbacks for attached multifamily developments
                     in a C-1, C-2 or I-1 District shall be 15 feet, except where located adjacent to a Residential Zoning
                     District the side and rear setbacks shall increase to 30 feet.
                (v) Building height shall be in conformance with the building height of the District in which the attached
                    multifamily development is proposed.
                (vi) A minimum building separation of 15 feet shall be provided between all buildings on the site.
                (vii) Attached multifamily development in all Districts must also meet the building design standards of
                      Section 8.04, the lighting design standards of Section 8.05, and the non-residential landscape
                      requirements of Section 9.03.
                (viii) Attached multifamily development in all Districts must also meet the common amenity area
                       requirements of Section 7.05 and the parkland dedication requirements of Section 15.08.
                (ix) Multifamily development existing prior to May 27, 2014, or depicted on a Site Plan approved prior
                     to May 27, 2014, shall be exempt from the requirements of the limitations of this section, except
                     that any expansion to that development shall require Special Use Permit approval in accordance
                     with this section.



138                                                                               Unified Development Code 2026
City of Georgetown                                                              Chapter 6. Zoning Use Regulations
Unified Development Code                                                                   Section 6.02. Use Tables

           g.   In addition to the requirements of f above, when reviewing the conceptual site layout required per
                Section 3.10, the City Council may consider and add conditions provided the requirements of the Zoning
                District are not exceeded, to the Special Use Permit including, but not limited to, the following:
                (i) Location of the development;
                (ii) Amount of lot frontage along a commercial corridor;
                (iii) Dwelling units per acre (maximum 24);
                (iv) Maximum building heights;
                (v) Dwelling units per structure;
                (vi) Type and number of amenities;
                (vii) Accessory structures;
                (viii) Ingress and egress locations; and
                (ix) Landscape buffers.
      4.   Accessory Dwelling Unit
           An accessory dwelling unit is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and Section 7.04, and subject to the
           following standards and limitations:
           a.   No more than one accessory dwelling unit per primary residence is permitted per lot.
           b.   An accessory dwelling unit is permitted as a subordinate use, provided that it is limited to 50% of the
                primary dwelling unit, and not to exceed 1,000 square feet.
           c.   A minimum of three parking spaces shall be available on-site providing the minimum two spaces
                required for the primary residence with one additional parking space provided for the accessory
                dwelling unit.
           d.   The accessory dwelling unit must remain on the same electric and water meters as the primary
                residence.
      5.   Second Dwelling Unit
           Within the AG, Agriculture District, in accordance with Section 6.02 , one additional primary dwelling unit
           may be constructed upon a lot or parcel for every 30 acres or portion thereof (i.e., one dwelling unit allowed
           for 30 acres or less, two dwelling units allowed for 31 acres or more, three dwelling units allowed for 61
           acres or more, etc.). The additional dwelling unit(s) is limited to use by an agricultural employee, a caretaker,
           family members, or guests of the property owner and must comply with all setback and design standards of
           the AG District.
      6.   Upper-Story Residential
           Upper-story residential dwellings are permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to the following
           standards and limitations:
           a.   The first floor shall not include the living space of any residential dwelling.
           b.   Separate designated parking spaces for the residential dwellings are required pursuant to Section 11.02.
           c.   Upper-story residential dwellings in the CN, I-1 Districts shall meet the following provisions in addition to
                Subsections a and b above:
                (i) The residential dwelling shall be secondary to the primary use.
                (ii) The gross floor area of the entire building shall not include more than 50% residential uses.




Unified Development Code 2026                                                                                             139
Chapter 6. Zoning Use Regulations                                                                City of Georgetown
Section 6.02. Use Tables                                                                 Unified Development Code

      7.   Home-Based Business
           Home-Based Businesses are permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to the standards and
           limitations:
           a.   Nothing in this section shall be applied or enforced to prohibit the operation of, or to require a license,
                permit, or other approval for, a no-impact Home-Base Business as defined by Section 229.902 of the
                Texas Local Government Code. The limitations in this section apply to a Home-Based Business only to the
                extent consistent with that section.
           b.   The Home-Based Business shall be conducted entirely within a dwelling unit or attached garage.
           c.   Neither the interior, nor the exterior of the dwelling unit shall be structurally altered so as to require
                compliance with nonresidential construction codes to accommodate the Home-Based Business. This
                provision shall not prohibit the construction of an accessory building as permitted by a residential zoning
                district.
           d.   The Home-Based Business shall not interfere with the use of the garage as a required parking space
                under this code.
           e.   No equipment, goods, supplies, or materials associated with the Home-Based Business shall be
                displayed or stored where visible from an abutting right-of-way or at the property line of an abutting
                property at a point six (6) feet above the finished grade.
           f.   The sale of merchandise directly to a customer on the premises is permitted; provided, however, the
                business does not generate on-street parking, a substantial increase in traffic, or activity visible from the
                street, and otherwise complies with the section.
           g.   The Home-Based Business shall not produce external noise, vibration, smoke, dust, odor, heat, glare,
                fumes, electrical interference, or waste runoff outside the dwelling unit or on the property surrounding
                the dwelling unit.
           h.   A Home-Based Business shall not generate more than 16 single directional vehicle trips each day of
                customer-related vehicular traffic, except that this limit shall not be applied to prohibit a no-impact
                Home-Based Business.
           i.   The total number of employees and customers on the premise at one time shall not exceed the
                applicable occupancy limits.
           j.   Signs shall meet the requirements of this code.

      B.   Civic Use Standards
           1.   All Civic Uses
                All Civic Uses as noted above, except Day Care, shall meet the following provisions, where applicable per
                Section 6.02. Uses that require a Special Use Permit, in accordance with Section 6.02, shall meet the
                following criteria in addition to securing said permit.
                a.   Any outdoor recreational playing field shall be set back 50 feet from any property line.
                b.   The principal vehicular entrance and exit shall be located on a collector-level street or higher, except as
                     otherwise approved by the Development Engineer.
           2.   Day Care
                Day care facilities are permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to the following standards and
                limitations:
                a.   All day care facilities shall be licensed by the state and meet the minimum requirements for such
                     facilities.
                b.   Outdoor play or instruction areas, playground equipment, and pools shall be located in the side or rear
                     yards and screened from adjacent property by an opaque fence no less than 6 feet in height.



142                                                                                       Unified Development Code 2026
City of Georgetown                                                           Chapter 6. Zoning Use Regulations
Unified Development Code                                                                Section 6.02. Use Tables

           c.   Day care facilities in Residential Zoning Districts may only operate between the hours of 6:00 a.m. and
                7:00 p.m. Day care facilities in CN Zoning Districts may only operate between the hours of 6:00 a.m. and
                10:00 p.m. Hours of operation are not limited for day care facilities in other Non-Residential Zoning
                Districts.
           d.   A family home day care shall employ only residents of the premises, including all paid and unpaid care
                providers.
           e.   A family home day care is allowed only one non-illuminated identification sign, provided the sign is
                mounted on the exterior wall of the dwelling and has an area no greater than 2 square feet.
      3.   Animal Shelter
           An animal shelter is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and limited to a required separation of at
           least 300 feet from the shelter to a residential structure that is located on any property in separate
           ownership.
      4.   Religious Assembly Facilities with Columbaria
           A columbaria, consistent with the definition of Texas Health and Safety Code § 711.008(b)(2), is permitted in
           accordance with Section 6.02 as an accessory use, subordinate and incidental to, a Religious Assembly
           Facility, subject to the following standards and limitations.
           a.   A columbaria located outdoors shall be subject to the following standards:
                (i) The columbaria shall be set back a minimum of 25 feet from the property line.
                (ii) The columbaria shall not exceed 8 feet in height.
                (iii) Landscaping shall be provided at a ratio of 2 square feet of landscaping for each square foot of
                      columbaria area, in addition to the minimum requirements of Chapter 9. Said landscaping shall be
                      incorporated into the overall design and placement of the columbaria.
           b.   The establishment of a columbaria shall be subject to Site Plan review pursuant to Section 3.17.
           c.   Upon discontinuance of the Religious Assembly Facility, the columbaria shall be relocated in compliance
                with all applicable state laws.

      B.     Transportation and Utility Use Standards
             1.   Heliports
                  Heliports are permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to the following standards and
                  limitations:
                  a.   A heliport may be utilized without a Special Use Permit only as an accessory use to a hospital or
                       government facility.
                  b.   A heliport may be utilized with a Special Use Permit in the following situations:
                       (i) An accessory use to a full-service hotel, office building, or convention center if the structure is over
                           100 feet in height and the heliport landing pad is located on the rooftop of such a structure; or
                       (ii) An accessory use to a business park that is a minimum of 40 total acres.

       2.     Utilities Services, Intermediate
              Intermediate Utility Services are permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to the following
              standards and limitations:
              a.   Any structure associated with the use shall be set back 25 feet from the property line of a residentially-
                   zoned property.
              b.   An enclosed fence or wall at least 6 feet in height shall be constructed at the boundaries of any structure
                   or apparatus associated with the use.
              c.   The intermediate utility use shall be screened with large evergreen shrubs planted 4 feet on center and
                   staggered 30 to 36 inches, located exterior to any required fencing.
              d.   The facility shall be secured.

   B.   Commercial Use Standards
        1.   Building Size Limitation
             a.   In the CN District, the floor-to-area ratio shall not exceed 0.3. The maximum building size of each
                  building on an individual lot or parcel shall be 7,500 square feet.
             b.   In the C-1 District, the floor-to-area ratio shall not exceed 0.5.
        2.   Bed and Breakfast
             A Bed and Breakfast establishment is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to the following
             standards and limitations:
             a.   All Districts
                  (i) No more than eight guestrooms per property shall be allowed, and if more than one building is
                      located on a Bed and Breakfast property, no more than six guestrooms shall be allowed in any one
                      building.
                  (ii) No food preparation, except beverages, is allowed within individual guestrooms. No stove, range,
                       hot plate, toaster oven, or microwave shall be allowed in any guestrooms; however, a small
                       microwave is permitted in outbuilding guest rooms.
                  (iii) Preparation and service of food shall conform to all applicable regulations of the State of Texas and
                        Williamson County.
                  (iv) The owner shall keep a current guest register including names, contact information, and dates of
                       occupancy for all guests.
                  (v) On-site parking (except driveways) shall not be located in the front yard and shall be screened from
                      the view of adjacent residences to a height of 6 feet by a solid screening fence or dense shrubs and
                      vegetation. Temporary fences shall not be permitted.
                  (vi) Guestroom rentals shall not be allowed for more than 15 consecutive days.
             b.   Residential Districts
                  Bed and Breakfast establishments in any residential District shall be subject to all of the standards and
                  limitations of Subsection a above. In addition, a Special Use Permit, pursuant to Section 3.10, is required
                  for a Bed and Breakfast establishment in any designated residential District and is subject to the
                  following conditions:
                  (i) The operator of the Bed and Breakfast must be a full-time resident of the main dwelling on the
                      property in which the Bed and Breakfast establishment is located.
                  (ii) Signage shall be restricted to one sign attached to the wall of the main dwelling that is a maximum
                       of 12 square feet, and one monument sign no larger than 6 square feet. However, the total signage
                       on the site shall not exceed 15 square feet. No additional advertising of any kind is allowed on site.


Unified Development Code 2026                                                                                              149
Chapter 6. Zoning Use Regulations                                                                City of Georgetown
Section 6.02. Use Tables                                                                 Unified Development Code

                (iii) Carriage houses, garage apartments, secondary free-standing houses, or similar dwellings that
                      contain a full service kitchen and are proposed to be used for Bed and Breakfast operations shall
                      remove the food preparation facilities prior to commencement of operation as a Bed and Breakfast.
      3.   Bed and Breakfast with Events
           A Bed and Breakfast with Events is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to the standards
           and limitations noted below. A Bed and Breakfast with Events applies only to properties on which a Bed and
           Breakfast is located, and events (such as parties, receptions, fund raisers, and other similar functions) are
           held. The event shall be a subordinate use to a Bed and Breakfast and shall not include an event center,
           meeting facility, or other form of entertainment operation.
           a.   All Districts
                (i) All provisions of Subsection 2 above shall also apply to Bed and Breakfasts with Events.
                (ii) The following additional conditions and limitations shall apply to Bed and Breakfasts with Events in
                     all permitted Districts:
                     (a) The Bed and Breakfast owner shall attend all events held on the property.
                     (b) The event hours, including set up and take down, shall be limited to the following:
                          •     Sunday through Thursday, 9:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m.
                          •     Friday and Saturday (and Sunday if it is a holiday weekend), 9:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m.
                     (c) Outdoor event areas shall not be located in the front yard and shall be screened from the view
                         of adjacent properties to a height of 6 feet by a solid screening fence or dense shrubs and
                         vegetation. Temporary fencing is not permitted.
           b.   Residential Districts
                Special Use Permit for Bed and Breakfast with Events shall be required in all residential Districts pursuant
                to Section 3.07, subject to Subsections 2 and a above, in addition to the following standards and
                limitations:
                (i) The Special Use Permit application for a Bed and Breakfast with Events shall include a description of
                    the proposed operation; the maximum number of events per year, month, and week; the
                    approximate number of attendees per event; hours of events and duration; location of the events
                    (indoor or outdoor); parking plans; security measures; traffic control plans; and sanitation
                    provisions.
                (ii) The City Council may add other conditions or limitations to the permit as it deems necessary in
                     order to manage the scale and scope of the proposed events, minimize the negative impacts of the
                     event(s) on the neighboring property owners, and protect the public health, safety, and welfare.
      4.   Hotel
           a.   A Special Use Permit for a hotel with more than 75 rooms shall be required in the Mixed-Use Downtown
                (MU-DT) Zoning District pursuant to Section 3.10.
      5.   Drive-Through
           The speaker boxes of any drive-through shall meet one of the following location criteria:
           a.   Located more than 150 feet of the nearest property line of a residentially zoned property or residentially
                used property in the ETJ; or
           b.   Positioned such that no speaker or microphone is facing toward a property line of a residentially zoned
                property or residentially used property in the ETJ.



150                                                                                 Unified Development Code 2026
City of Georgetown                                                            Chapter 6. Zoning Use Regulations
Unified Development Code                                                                 Section 6.02. Use Tables

           c.   The below elements shall be completely screened from view at an adjoining property line of a
                residentially zoned property or, in the ETJ, a residentially used property. Screening shall be provided by a
                wall or other screening mechanism, not less than 8 feet in height, that has a similar finish to the primary
                structure. Screening shall be required for the following elements of Drive-Throughs:
                (i) Queuing spaces
                (ii) Order boxes
                (iii) Order window
                (iv) Drive-through pick up windows
      6.   Bar, Tavern or Pub, Dance Hall or Nightclub
           A bar, tavern, pub, dance hall, or nightclub is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to the
           following standards and limitations:
           a.   The establishment shall be located no less than 300 feet from a church, public or private school or public
                hospital, subject to the measurements of the City Code of Ordinances.
           b.   The establishment is subject to the provisions of Chapter 6.40, Alcoholic Beverages, of the City Code of
                Ordinances.
      7.   Micro Brewery, Micro Winery or Micro Distillery
           A micro brewery, micro winery, or micro distillery is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to
           the following standards and limitations:
           a.   A micro brewery, micro winery, or micro distillery shall be located no less than 300 feet from a church,
                public or private school or public hospital subject to the measurements of the City Code of Ordinances.
           b.   A micro brewery, micro winery, or micro distillery is subject to the provisions of Chapter 6.40, Alcoholic
                Beverages, of the City Code of Ordinances.
      8.   Permanent Mobile or Outdoor Food Vendor
           Permanent Mobile or Outdoor Food Vendor is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to the
           following standards and limitations:
           a.   The Mobile or Outdoor Food Vendor(s) shall be a primary use on the property.
           b.   Each Mobile or Outdoor Food Vendor must comply with applicable building, fire, plumbing, electrical,
                and health regulations related to utility service, consistent with state law.
           c.   A Mobile Food Park Manager shall be designated for the property.
                (i) The Mobile Food Park Manager shall be available by phone while the vendor(s) is open for business.
                    A telephone number and email address for the Mobile Food Park Manager shall be posted on a sign
                    no larger than 1 square foot. The sign shall be posted on a location visible to the patrons.
                (ii) The Mobile Food Park Manager shall be responsible for the general management of the park
                     including, but not limited to addressing inquiries, questions, and concerns, ensuring property
                     maintenance, enforcing hours of operation, and other operational matters.
           d.   Parking shall be provided in accordance with Chapter 11 of this Code.
           e.   Toilet facilities and trash receptacles shall be provided on the property in compliance with all applicable
                City regulations.
           f.   Amenities including but not limited to tables, chairs and shade structures may be permitted on the
                property subject to compliance with this Code.




Unified Development Code 2026                                                                                             151
Chapter 6. Zoning Use Regulations                                                                City of Georgetown
Section 6.02. Use Tables                                                                 Unified Development Code

           g.   All vendors, amenities and other site improvements shall be identified on any development plans
                otherwise required for the property under this Code.
      9.   Live Music, Entertainment, or Event Facility
           a.   The entertainment use must be secondary to the primary use in the C-1 and MU-DT Districts.
           b.   Any live music, event facility and/or entertainment venue must maintain a minimum setback of 100 feet
                from any residential use.
           c.   Live music, event facility or entertainment uses are subject to the provisions of Chapter 8.16, Noise, of
                the Georgetown Municipal Code.
      10. Theater, Movie or Live
           A movie theater or live theater is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 provided that the theater may
           not have more than eight screens.
      11. Athletic Facilities, Commercial Recreation and Driving Ranges
           a.   Athletic facilities, commercial recreation facilities, and driving ranges are permitted in accordance with
                Section 6.02 provided that any outdoor playing fields or associated structures shall be set back 50 feet
                from the property line of a residentially-zoned property.
           b.   In the C-1 District, uses may only occur indoors.
      12. General Office, Integrated Office Center, and Health Services
           a.   General Office in the RS District
                A general office use is permitted in the RS District in accordance with Section 6.02 and is subject to the
                following standards and limitations, which allow for an orderly transition of land use from residential to
                small-scale office while maintaining residential appearance and building scale:
                (i) Only a house meeting the following criteria is eligible to apply for a Special Use Permit, pursuant to
                    Section 3.10, for an office use in the RS District:
                    (a) The house is located in the RS District;
                    (b) The house existed on or before February 26, 2008 (the date adopting the ordinance); and
                    (c) The house has a side lot line immediately adjacent to property zoned as C-1, C-3 or I-1 District
                        that is used for commercial or industrial uses and developed without a bufferyard.
                    (d) A residential side lot line of less than 30% shall not qualify as a side lot line for the above
                        adjacency requirement.
                (ii) In addition to the requirements for Special Use Permits set forth in Section 3.07, an applicant for a
                     Special Use Permit under this section shall also submit a Site Plan pursuant to the requirements of
                     Section 3.09. Further, an interior layout of the building shall be submitted with the Special Use
                     Permit application.
                (iii) Off-street parking shall be provided at one-and-one-half spaces per habitable room. For the
                      purposes of this section, a habitable room includes foyers and lofts if used for reception areas, work
                      stations, offices, conference rooms, etc., but excludes restrooms, kitchens, porches (enclosed or
                      open), and utility rooms. This parking requirement is in place of the parking requirement in Table
                      11.02.040-1. Off-Street Parking Requirements*. All parking shall be paved and approaches shall be
                      concrete.

            (iv) Parking shall not be permitted in the front yard. An exception to this provision may be considered
                 with the Special Use Permit related to preserving Protected and Heritage Trees or to recognize
                 existing garages or parking areas. Parking shall be screened from view of the right-of-way in

            (v) A solid screening wall or fence or dense shrubs and vegetation at least 6 feet in height shall be

                including parking, and as the fence approaches the right-of-way.
            (vi) A Building Permit may be required prior to issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy.

                  preventative or corrective personal treatment services by doctors or similar practitioners of medical

                  centers are not permitted uses.
            (viii) The use of the property for counseling in an office setting by a psychologist or psychiatrist is a
                   permitted office use.
            (ix) The City Council may consider approval of a lesser office use that would occupy only a portion of a
                 house. If only a portion of the structure is used, reduced standards may be applied, especially for a
                 "live/work" use of a house.
            (x) A Special Use Permit issued under this section shall contain the following special conditions, at a
                minimum. The City Council may include other special conditions of the permit on a case-by-case
                basis.
                (a) The office use shall be conducted entirely within the main structure or integral part thereof and
                    have no outdoor storage of any kind.
                (b) Office uses are not permitted in any accessory building.
                (c) Uses accessory to office uses are prohibited, except a conference room may be established for
                    an on-site office.

                      (d) On-site sales are prohibited.
                      (e) Outdoor storage is prohibited; however, the interior of any accessory structures may be used

                      (f) The number of workers shall be limited to the number of habitable rooms (excluding restrooms,

                      (g) No exterior evidence of the office use shall be allowed, except for one non-internally

                      (h) Business hours and regular deliveries by commercial vehicle (excluding 18 wheeled vehicles,

                      (i) A Temporary Use Permit in accordance with Section 3.10 is required for any party, reception,

                          (including tenants). Parties, receptions, events or similar functions, subject to the Temporary
                          Use Permit provision, shall be limited to a total of six such functions per calendar year. Such
                          events shall be limited to the interior of the structure.
                      (j) The Special Use Permit shall be null and void if the structure is damaged by natural or
                          accidental causes to the extent of more than 50% of the value of the structure on the date of
                          the damage, and if it is not rebuilt in-kind within 14 months or the use of the structure for
                          office uses has been discontinued for a period of 12 months or more. The 14-month period
                          does not include the period of time necessary to conclude any litigation related to such
                          calamity.
                      (k) Increased run-off resulting from conversion to office use shall be detained on-site or shall be
                          diverted from adjacent property in conformance with the stormwater drainage requirements of
                          this Code.
                      (l) The total impervious cover shall not exceed the requirements of the RS District.
      13. Data Center
          a.   Where Permitted.
               (i)      A data center is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 in the C-2, Regional Commercial Zoning
                        District provided that the total floor area of all building(s) does not exceed 5,000 square feet, and
                        subject to the specific development standards in subsection b. below except for (b)(iv).
               (ii)     A data center is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 in the I-1, Flex Industrial Zoning District
                        and I-2, Intensive Industrial Zoning District, subject to the specific development standards in
                        subsection b. below.
          b. Data Center Standards. The following standards shall apply to all data centers where such are allowed
          and approved:
               (i)      Setbacks. All buildings, including accessory structures and outdoor equipment used for data
                        centers, shall be a minimum of 250 feet from the nearest residential zoning district or use,
                        whether inside the City Limits or the ETJ.
               (ii)     Bufferyards. Notwithstanding Section 9.03.070 of this UDC, a high level bufferyard shall always be
                        required, except that a minimum 8-foot tall screening wall constructed of brick, stone, reinforced
                        concrete or other similar two-sided masonry materials shall be required, and as a minimum, the


154                                                                                 Unified Development Code 2026
City of Georgetown                                                            Chapter 6. Zoning Use Regulations
Unified Development Code                                                                 Section 6.02. Use Tables

                      required shade trees in Section 9.03.070 shall first be placed along the lot line(s) facing any
                      residential use or zoning district at a minimum of one (1) tree for every 40 linear feet. Any
                      additional trees required beyond this amount may be placed anywhere in the bufferyard.
               (iii) Parking. Data centers shall provide a minimum of one (1) parking space per 400 square feet of
                     office area. Data center storage and computing areas not occupied by employees shall be exempt
                     from any parking requirements.
               (iv) Noise. The applicant shall submit a noise attenuation study prepared by a licensed professional
                    engineer specializing in noise acoustics and/or certified by the International Institute of Noise
                    Control Engineering that addresses maximum sound levels including low frequency noise levels.
                    (a) Data centers must comply with noise limits as outlined in Section 8.16.030 of the City Code of
                    Ordinances. In the C2 district, a data center is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 provided
                    that the building size does not exceed 5,000 square feet.
      14. General Retail
          General retail is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to the following standards and
          limitations:
          a.   In the MU-DT District.
               (i) A Special Use Permit is required for any retail building exceeding 40,000 square feet.
      15. Kennel
          A kennel is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to the following standards and limitations:
          a.   The kennel operation, including all structures, is required to be at least 100 feet from the property line of
               a residentially zoned property.
          b.   Outdoor kennels are prohibited in the C-2 District.
      16. Self-Storage, Indoor and Outdoor
          An indoor or outdoor self-storage establishment is permitted in accordance with 6.02.080 and subject to the
          following standards and limitations:
          a.   Self-storage facilities shall be limited to the storage use only, with the exception of an accessory leasing
               office, accessory retail sales, and/or single living quarters for security purposes, and shall not be used for
               operating any other business. In no instance shall individual storage units be used as a business
               storefront or used as a residence or overnight accommodation.
          b.   Indoor self-storage facilities shall operate completely within a building or structure.
          c.   Indoor self-storage facilities shall be limited to climate-controlled facilities accessed solely from shared
               interior hallways.
          d.   Storage bay doors shall not face a public right-of-way unless set back a minimum of 40 feet from the
               property line.
          e.   Each individual outdoor storage unit shall be directly accessible from an apron consisting of an approved
               paved surface.
          f.   Where gated, a minimum of 60 feet of driveway shall be provided between the public right-of-way and
               the front gate of the self-storage facility.
          g.   Outdoor storage shall not include the storage of wrecked or inoperable vehicles.
          h.   No outdoor self-storage shall be permitted within a required setback.




Unified Development Code 2026                                                                                                 155
Chapter 6. Zoning Use Regulations                                                              City of Georgetown
Section 6.02. Use Tables                                                               Unified Development Code

          i.   No outdoor self-storage shall be allowed in required off-street parking areas. Areas intended for outdoor
               self-storage shall be paved and painted to distinguish them from required off-street parking areas.
          j.   Outdoor self-storage shall be screened from any public right-of-way by an 8-foot-tall screening wall.
      17. Pest Control or Janitorial Services
          A pest control or janitorial services facility is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to the
          following standards and limitations:
          a.   No mixing of chemicals or pesticides is allowed on-site.
          b.   Storage of chemicals or pesticides is limited to 10% of the total square footage of the primary facility.
          c.   No overnight vehicle or outdoor storage is allowed.
      18. Office/Showroom
          An Office/Showroom is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to the following standards
          and limitations:
          a.   Warehousing facilities shall be incidental to the primary use and shall not exceed 10% of the total floor
               area.
          b.   Outdoor storage may be permitted in accordance with Section 6.02.080.
      19. Automobile Sales, Rental or Leasing Facility
          An automobile sales, rental or leasing facility is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to the
          following standards and limitations:
          a.   Lighting
               Fixed lighting shall be shielded or have cut-off fixtures to prevent direct glare of beams onto any
               adjacent public or private property or street. Light poles shall be placed no closer than 45 feet apart.
          b.   Auto Repair and Service
               Automobile Repair and Service, Limited and General, shall be an allowed accessory use with an
               Automobile Sales Facility. Automobile Repair and Service, General shall not be permitted on the
               premises of a Rental Vehicle Facility and any allowed limited repairs shall be performed only within the
               principal building.
          c.   Screening from Residential
               Screening that meets the High Level Bufferyard standards shall be installed along all lot lines that abut or
               are adjacent to a Residential District, an existing single-family home in the AG District, or an existing
               single-family home in the ETJ that is platted and designated for residential use on the Future Land Use
               Map. The screening must block views of the use, its operations, and any stored or displayed vehicles,
               materials, or equipment from all ground-level vantage points on the adjacent residential property.
          d.   Outdoor Display and Storage
               (i) Display and storage areas shall be clearly shown on the Site Plan and identified on the site.
               (ii) Outdoor display of vehicles shall be set back a minimum of 25 feet from all lot lines abutting
                    residentially zoned or developed property.
               (iii) Temporary overflow vehicle storage is allowed on paved surfaces only. This temporary storage shall
                     not impede the traffic flow of the site or eliminate required parking spaces.
               (iv) Permanent and temporary tent canopies may be erected over areas used for automobile sales
                    display and shall not be considered buildings, but may not encroach into building setbacks, required
                    parking spaces or drive aisles. All necessary Building Permits shall be required, but a revision to an


156                                                                               Unified Development Code 2026
City of Georgetown                                                            Chapter 6. Zoning Use Regulations
Unified Development Code                                                                 Section 6.02. Use Tables

                   existing Site Plan shall not be required if the tent canopy is located over an existing display area. All
                   safety issues regarding fire and building codes shall be addressed.
          e.   Signage for Automobile Sales Facilities
               The following additional signage applies only to automobile sales facilities along the I.H. 35 northbound
               frontage road, from the southernmost boundary of the City up to, and including, the one lot north of Fox
               Drive.
               (i) High profile monument signs are encouraged for sites with multiple corporate tenants consistent
                   with Subsection 12.05.060. Auto dealerships may have an increased height for a high profile
                   monument sign located along the I-35 frontage road of up to 35 feet. No more than one sign shall
                   be permitted at the 35-foot height. No additional height shall be permitted. The structure of high
                   profile monument signs shall be constructed of stone or brick materials and be colors compatible
                   with those utilized on the primary building's façade.
               (ii) Additional high profile monument signage shall be allowed for those sites with multiple corporate
                    tenants. The maximum amount of additional signage shall be limited to an increase of 10% of the
                    total pole sign square footage permitted in Chapter 12. The maximum high profile monument sign
                    height that utilizes the increased size shall be limited to 28 feet. The minimum road frontage of 600
                    feet for a high profile monument sign is reduced to 250 feet for this section and the spacing of 600
                    feet between high profile monument signs shall be reduced to 250 feet for this section.
               (iii) A maximum of two high profile monument or pole signs per site are permitted for sites with
                     multiple corporate tenants with the maximum sign height of 25 feet and a maximum of 100 square
                     feet per sign.
               (iv) For those sites with multiple corporate tenants the allowed wall signage may be increased 10% to
                    accommodate the additional tenant.
               (v) In accordance with Section 12.03, entrance and interior directional signs that comply with the
                   provisions of Chapter 12 shall not be counted toward the total allowed signage for the site.
               (vi) No signs, balloons, banners, etc. shall be located within the public right-of-way.
               (vii) Balloons.
                   (a) For the purposes of this section, balloons shall not be deemed as fluttering/undulating/moving
                       signs pursuant to Section 12.04.
                   (b) Balloons shall be tethered, attached, or anchored so as not to create any safety hazards by
                       blowing into signs, utility lines, lights, etc.
                   (c) Balloons and their tethering mechanism shall not exceed 35 feet in height.
                   (d) Balloons for vehicle sales facilities shall not exceed a total of 50 balloons per 100 feet of I-35
                       road frontage.
      20. Commercial Vehicle Sales, Rental or Leasing Facility
          Commercial Vehicle Sales, Rental or Leasing Facility is permitted with Section 6.02 and subject to the
          following standards and limitations:
          a.   Lighting
               Fixed lighting shall be shielded or have cut-off fixtures to prevent direct glare of beams onto any
               adjacent public or private property or street. Light poles shall be placed no closer than 45 feet apart.
          b.   Screening from Residential

               Screening that meets the High Level Bufferyard standards shall be provided along all lot lines that abut
               or are adjacent to a Residential District, an existing single-family home in the AG District, or an existing
               single-family home in the ETJ that is platted and planned for residential use on the Future Land Use Map.
          c.   Outdoor Display and Storage
               (i) Display and storage areas shall be clearly shown on the Site Plan and identified on the site.
               (ii) Outdoor display of commercial vehicles shall be set back a minimum of 25 feet from all lot lines
                    abutting residentially zoned or developed property.
               (iii) Outdoor storage shall be located behind the front building façade of the primary structure.
               (iv) Permanent and temporary tent canopies may be erected over areas used for automobile sales
                    display and shall not be considered buildings, but may not encroach into building setbacks, required
                    parking spaces, drive aisles or bufferyards. All necessary Building Permits shall be required, but a
                    revision to an existing Site Plan shall not be required if the tent canopy is located over an existing
                    display area. All safety issues regarding fire and building codes shall be addressed.
          d.   Accessory Uses
               Automobile Repair and Service, Limited and General, and Automobile Parts and Accessory Sales, Indoor,
               shall be allowed accessory uses with a Commercial Vehicle Sales Facility. Automobile Repair and Service,
               General shall not be permitted on the premises of a Rental Facility and any allowed limited repairs shall
               be performed only within the principal building.
      21. Automobile Repair and Service, General
          a.   In the General Commercial (C-2) District, temporary outdoor storage of automobiles awaiting service or
               pick-up is permitted within the guidelines specified in Subsection 6.02.080. No other outdoor storage is
               allowed in the C-2 District.
          b.   In the I-2 District, all outdoor storage, except as limited in Subsection 6.02.080, is permitted.
      22. Fuel Sales
          A fuel sales establishment is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 , subject to the standards of Section
          3.10, and subject to the following standards and limitations:
          a.   The use shall generally not abut a single-family residential zoned or used property without attention to
               the impact of screening, buffering, and lighting to the adjacent residential uses.
          b.   Proximity to other developed or entitled fuel sales facilities shall be examined as part of the Special Use
               Permit process to avoid clustering of uses along a corridor, intersection, or neighborhood. No more than
               two fuel sales facilities shall be permitted at any intersection and only when located diagonally on
               opposite corners
          c.   No more than four multi-fuel dispensers (eight fuel positions) shall be permitted except where one of
               the following conditions is met:
               (i) The property is located on a corner of a major arterial roadway and a collector or higher level
                   roadway as classified in the Future Mobility Plan (FMP); or
               (ii) The proposed fuel sales establishment is an accessory use to a commercial development such as a
                    grocery store or retail center with a gross floor area of 50,000 square feet or more; or
               (iii) The property is adjacent to the SH 130 Toll or I-35 roadways.
          d.   When one of the conditions outlined in Subsection c above is met, in no case shall a fuel sales
               establishment be permitted more than 10 multi-fuel dispensers or 20 fuel positions.
          e.   Proximity to Residential:


158                                                                                  Unified Development Code 2026
City of Georgetown                                                            Chapter 6. Zoning Use Regulations
Unified Development Code                                                                 Section 6.02. Use Tables

               (i) Fuel Sales canopies and fuel pumps of a fuel sales use may not be located within 200 feet of a
                   residentially zoned property, or an existing residential property located in the ETJ.
          f.   An 8-foot wall shall be required at the property line of residentially zoned property or residentially used
               property located in the ETJ, in addition to the required bufferyards in Subsection 9.03.070.
          g.   Fuel positions, vacuum, air, and water stations as well as other similar equipment are prohibited
               between the principal structure and the property line of a residentially-zoned property or a residentially
               used property within the ETJ and shall comply with the building setbacks in all other circumstances.
          h.   The bottom of the canopy shall be a minimum of 13 feet 6 inches in height.
          i.   In addition to the requirements in Section 8.05, any freestanding light fixtures shall be reduced in height
               to 15 feet if the use is adjacent to a residential District.
          j.   No full-service or self-service car wash is allowed with the fuel sales use. Only an accessory one-bay
               automatic car wash is allowed.
      23. Fuel Sales with More than 10 Multi-Fuel Dispensers
          A Special Use Permit for a fuel sales establishment with more than 10 multi-fuel dispensers (20 fuel
          positions) shall be required in the General Commercial (C-2) and I-2 Zoning District pursuant to Section 3.10,
          and subject to the standards in Subsections 22.a through 22.i above.
      24. Car Wash
          The consideration of a car wash is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02, subject to the standards of
          Section 3.07 - Special Use Permit, and following standards and limitations:
          a.   A self-service car wash facility may contain a maximum of four self-service bays.
          b.   A fuel sales use is not allowed with either a full-service or self-service car wash.
          c.   The use shall not abut a single-family residential zoned or used property.
          d.   Proximity to other developed or entitled car wash facilities shall be examined as part of the Special Use
               Permit process to avoid clustering of uses along a corridor, intersection, or neighborhood.
          e.   The order boxes of any drive-through shall meet one of the following location criteria:
               (i) Located more than 150 feet of the nearest property line of a residentially zoned property or
                   residentially used property in the ETJ; or
               (ii) Positioned such that no speaker or microphone is facing toward a property line of a residentially
                    zoned property or residentially used property in the ETJ.
          f.   The below elements shall be completely screened from view at an adjoining property line of a
               residentially zoned property or, in the ETJ, a residentially used property. Screening shall be provided by a
               wall or other screening mechanism, not less than 8 feet in height, that has a similar finish to the primary
               structure. Screening shall be required for the following elements of Drive-Throughs:
               (i) Queuing spaces
               (ii) Order boxes
               (iii) Order window
               (iv) Drive-through pick up windows
      25. Towing Services and Impound Lots
          A Towing Services and Impound Lot use may be permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to the
          following standards and limitations:

   B.   Industrial Use Standards
        1.   Contractor Services, Limited
             Contractor Services, Limited is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to the following
             standards and limitations:
             a.   Parking spaces shall be provided for fleet vehicles in addition to the minimum number of parking spaces
                  required per Chapter 11 of this Code.
             b.   Parking of fleet vehicles shall comply with the Outdoor Storage, Limited requirements of Subsection
                  6.02.080.B.2.
             c.   When the outdoor storage area is gated, a minimum of two vehicle stacking spaces from the key code
                  box shall be provided. Vehicle stacking spaces shall comply with Section 11.05.
        2.   Contractor Services, General
             Contractor Services, General is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to the following
             standards and limitations:
             a.   Outdoor storage shall be incidental to the primary use and may be permitted in accordance with Section
                  6.02.080.
             b.   Outdoor storage may be increased to 50% of the total site area provided the outdoor storage area is not
                  located adjacent to a public street, residential zoned property, an existing single-family home in the ETJ
                  that is platted or designated for residential use on the Future Land Use Map, or a public park.
             c.   When outdoor storage is proposed to be located adjacent to a public street, residential zoned property,
                  an existing single-family home in the ETJ that is platted or designated for residential use on the Future
                  Land Use Map, or a public park, articulation shall be provided for the screening wall or fence by one of
                  the following:
                  (i) Columns or similar column effect as approved by the Director, using different materials than the
                      wall, spaced no more than 125 feet apart; or
                  (ii) Variations in depth achieved either through offsets of at least 5 feet deep, plant material groupings,
                       breaks in walls, or other variations as approved by the Director, occurring every 80 feet.
             d.   Fleet vehicles shall be parked in the same area as the designated outdoor storage to be screened from
                  the public.
             e.   When the outdoor storage area is gated, a minimum of two vehicle stacking spaces from the key code
                  box shall be provided. Vehicle stacking spaces shall comply with Section 11.05.
        3.   Office/Warehouse
             Office/Warehouse is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to the following standards and
             limitations:
             a.   The primary entrance shall be located in the office portion of the building.
             b.   The warehouse portion may not exceed more than 50% of the front building façade.
             c.   Access to the loading and storage areas shall be limited to the side or rear of the building.


Unified Development Code 2026                                                                                              161
Chapter 6. Zoning Use Regulations                                                                     City of Georgetown
Section 6.02. Use Tables                                                                      Unified Development Code

                d.   The use is limited to a single loading dock/door.
           4.   Storage Yard
                Storage Yard is permitted in accordance with Section 6.02 and subject to the following standards and
                limitations:
                a.   All equipment, material and any other outdoor storage shall be located on an approved paved surface.
                b.   All equipment, material and any other outdoor storage shall comply with the setback requirements of
                     the District, and the landscape standards of Chapter 9.
                     (i) For purposes of this subsection, street yard trees shall be provided between the screen wall and the
                         street lot line.
                c.   When outdoor storage is proposed to be located adjacent to a public street, residential zoned property,
                     an existing single-family home in the ETI that is platted or designated for residential use on the Future
                     Land Use Map, or a public park, articulation shall be provided for the screening wall or fence by one of
                     the following:
                     (i) Masonry columns or similar column effect as approved by the Director, using different materials
                         than the wall, spaced no more than 125 feet apart; or
                     (ii) Variations in depth achieved either through offsets of at least 5 feet deep, plant material groupings,
                          breaks in walls, or other variations as approved by the Director, occurring every 80 feet.
                d.   When outdoor storage areas are gated, a minimum of two vehicle stacking spaces from the key code box
                     shall be provided. Vehicle stacking spaces shall comply with Section 11.05.
                e.   Outdoor storage shall comply with the requirements of Section 6.02.080.
